stem: A startup is evaluating a move to AWS. Which TWO of the following are commonly cited advantages of cloud computing over running your own data center? (Select TWO.)
options: Trade capital expense for variable expense, paying only for the compute you consume instead of buying servers up front.
You must forecast and purchase enough hardware capacity for your highest expected peak load, months in advance.
You take on full responsibility for maintaining and replacing the physical data center facilities.
Benefit from massive economies of scale, since AWS aggregates usage from hundreds of thousands of customers to lower the pay-as-you-go price.
You must sign a multi-year contract before the first server can be provisioned.
explanation: Trading capital expense for variable expense means paying for compute as you use it instead of buying racks of servers ahead of demand, and economies of scale let AWS pass its purchasing volume on to customers as lower pay-as-you-go prices. Forecasting peak capacity months ahead is exactly the guessing game the cloud removes. AWS, not the customer, operates and maintains the physical facilities under the shared responsibility model. AWS services can be provisioned on demand with no long-term contract required.

stem: AWS aggregates the usage of hundreds of thousands of customers to negotiate better pricing from suppliers and pass the resulting savings on as lower pay-as-you-go rates. Which cloud computing benefit does this describe?
options: Economies of scale
Elasticity
High availability
Fault tolerance
explanation: Economies of scale is the benefit where aggregating demand across a huge customer base lets AWS negotiate lower supplier costs and pass the savings to customers. Elasticity is the ability to automatically add or remove capacity to match demand, not a pricing effect. High availability and fault tolerance describe a system's ability to keep running through failures, not AWS's purchasing power.

stem: A retail website's traffic spikes sharply during flash sales and drops back to normal afterward. The company wants its infrastructure to automatically add capacity during the spike and automatically remove that capacity afterward, so it never pays for idle servers. Which cloud characteristic provides this?
options: Scalability, which only refers to the maximum size a system can be manually grown to
Elasticity, which automatically scales resources out and in to match real-time demand
Durability, which describes the likelihood that stored data will not be lost
Consolidated billing, which combines charges from multiple accounts onto one invoice
explanation: Elasticity is the ability of a cloud environment to automatically scale compute resources out to meet a demand spike and back in once demand falls, so the company pays only for what it actually uses. Scalability describes the capability to grow (or shrink) a system's capacity, but on its own does not imply the automatic, real-time adjustment elasticity provides. Durability is about data not being lost, not about compute capacity. Consolidated billing is a billing feature, unrelated to capacity changes.

stem: A company based in one country wants to deploy its application closer to customers in several other countries to reduce latency, and do so within minutes rather than the months of lead time it would take to build new facilities. Which cloud computing benefit does AWS provide for this?
options: Consolidated billing across linked accounts
The shared responsibility model
The ability to go global in minutes by deploying into AWS Regions around the world
Reserved Instance pricing discounts
explanation: Going global in minutes is the AWS benefit of deploying an application into additional Regions around the world in a few clicks, instead of the months or years it would take to build new physical data centers. Consolidated billing only merges invoices and has nothing to do with geographic reach. The shared responsibility model defines who secures what, not global deployment speed. Reserved Instance pricing is a discount model, not a deployment capability.

stem: A team wants a structured way to review whether their workload is right-sized, whether they are using the most cost-effective services, and whether spending is being tracked and controlled over time. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar addresses this?
options: Operational Excellence
Reliability
Performance Efficiency
Cost Optimization
explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs, right-sizing resources, choosing the most cost-effective pricing models, and tracking spend over time. Operational Excellence covers running and monitoring systems to deliver business value, not cost control. Reliability covers a workload's ability to recover from disruptions. Performance Efficiency covers using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements, which is related but distinct from managing cost.

stem: A company wants its workload to recover quickly from the failure of an individual component, an Availability Zone, or an entire Region, and to automatically recover from infrastructure or service disruptions. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar covers this design goal?
options: Reliability
Security
Cost Optimization
Sustainability
explanation: The Reliability pillar covers a workload's ability to perform its function correctly and consistently, including recovering from infrastructure or service disruptions and dynamically acquiring resources to meet demand. Security covers protecting data and systems, not recovery from failure. Cost Optimization is about avoiding unnecessary spend. Sustainability is about minimizing the environmental impact of running workloads, not failure recovery.

stem: A team is deciding between several EC2 instance families and storage options to ensure their workload uses computing resources efficiently as demand and technology change over time. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar covers this decision?
options: Operational Excellence
Performance Efficiency
Security
Cost Optimization
explanation: Performance Efficiency covers using computing resources efficiently to meet requirements, and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes and technology evolves, which includes choosing the right instance types and storage. Operational Excellence is about running and monitoring systems and continually improving processes, not resource selection. Security covers protection of data and systems. Cost Optimization focuses on spend rather than resource-to-workload fit.

stem: A team wants to run and monitor systems to deliver business value, and continually improve their processes and procedures through automation, runbooks, and small frequent changes. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar covers this?
options: Reliability
Cost Optimization
Operational Excellence
Security
explanation: Operational Excellence covers running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improving supporting processes, including automating changes, responding to events, and defining standards through runbooks. Reliability is about recovering from disruptions rather than the operating processes themselves. Cost Optimization is about spend. Security is about protecting data and systems, a separate pillar from day-to-day operations.

stem: AWS added a sixth pillar to the Well-Architected Framework focused on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads, such as maximizing resource utilization and reducing energy consumption. Which pillar is this?
options: Performance Efficiency
Reliability
Cost Optimization
Sustainability
explanation: The Sustainability pillar addresses the long-term environmental impact of a workload, such as energy and resource efficiency. Performance Efficiency is about matching resources to workload needs generally, not environmental impact specifically. Reliability is about resilience to failure. Cost Optimization is about avoiding unnecessary spend, which can overlap with efficiency but is a distinct financial pillar, not the environmental one.

stem: Within a single AWS Region, AWS operates multiple discrete data centers, each with independent power, cooling, and networking, connected by low-latency links so an application can run across more than one for higher availability. What are these individual locations called?
options: Availability Zones
Edge locations
Local Zones
Wavelength Zones
explanation: Availability Zones are one or more discrete data centers within a Region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking, connected through low-latency links so workloads can span multiple zones for fault tolerance. Edge locations are the smaller sites used by Amazon CloudFront to cache content close to users, not full data centers. Local Zones and Wavelength Zones extend AWS infrastructure closer to specific metro areas or telecom networks, but they are not the base building block of a Region.

stem: A company runs its production database on Amazon RDS and wants it to keep serving requests with minimal downtime even if the entire data center hosting the primary database instance becomes unavailable. Which RDS feature BEST meets this need?
options: Read replicas in the same Availability Zone as the primary instance
A Multi-AZ deployment, which maintains a synchronously replicated standby in a different Availability Zone and fails over automatically
A larger instance class for the existing single database instance
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication for the database's storage volume
explanation: An RDS Multi-AZ deployment keeps a synchronously replicated standby in a separate Availability Zone and automatically fails over to it if the primary becomes unavailable, minimizing downtime. Read replicas in the same zone do not protect against a zone-level failure and are mainly for offloading read traffic. A bigger instance class improves performance, not availability during an outage. S3 Cross-Region Replication applies to S3 objects, not an RDS database's storage volume.

stem: A media company wants to cache its video thumbnails and static assets at locations physically close to end users around the world, so requests are served with lower latency than if they always traveled back to the origin Region. Which AWS capability provides this?
options: AWS Direct Connect
AWS Transit Gateway
Amazon CloudFront using edge locations
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
explanation: Amazon CloudFront is AWS's content delivery network, and it caches content at globally distributed edge locations so end users are served from a nearby cache instead of the origin, cutting latency. Direct Connect is a dedicated private network link to AWS, not a caching layer. Transit Gateway interconnects VPCs and on-premises networks. Site-to-Site VPN provides an encrypted tunnel between a customer network and AWS, and neither of those caches content near end users.

stem: A company runs a real-time bidding application that must process requests from mobile devices with single-digit-millisecond latency by running compute inside a telecommunications provider's 5G network, as close to end users' devices as possible. Which AWS infrastructure offering is purpose-built for this?
options: AWS Local Zones, which place compute and storage in large metropolitan areas near end users
AWS Outposts, which extends AWS infrastructure into a customer's own data center
Additional Availability Zones within the nearest AWS Region
AWS Wavelength, which embeds AWS compute and storage inside telecommunications providers' 5G networks
explanation: AWS Wavelength embeds AWS compute and storage services within telecommunications providers' 5G networks, so traffic from mobile and connected devices reaches the application without leaving the telecom network, achieving the lowest possible latency for mobile edge use cases. Local Zones bring AWS infrastructure closer to large population and industry centers but do not run inside a telecom's 5G network specifically. Outposts extends AWS into a customer's own data center, not a telecom network. Adding more Availability Zones in the nearest Region does not reduce the last-mile mobile network latency the way running inside the 5G network does.

stem: A company wants to move an on-premises application to AWS as quickly as possible with the least amount of change, by moving each server to an equivalent EC2 instance without modifying the application's architecture. Which of the 6 R's migration strategies does this describe?
options: Rehost (lift-and-shift)
Refactor / re-architect
Replatform
Retire
explanation: Rehost, often called lift-and-shift, moves an application to the cloud with no code changes, typically mapping existing servers to equivalent EC2 instances, which is usually the fastest migration path. Refactor (re-architect) involves redesigning the application to take advantage of cloud-native features, which is more effort, not less. Replatform makes some cloud optimizations, such as swapping to a managed database, which is more change than a pure lift-and-shift. Retire means decommissioning an application that is no longer needed, not moving it.

stem: During migration planning, a team decides to move its on-premises MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL, changing where backups, patching, and Multi-AZ failover are managed, but keeping the same schema and application code. Which of the 6 R's does this represent?
options: Repurchase, because moving to a managed database means buying a new commercial license
Replatform, which makes a targeted cloud optimization like adopting a managed database without changing the application's core architecture
Rehost, because both moving to RDS and redesigning the architecture involve zero code changes
Retain, because the database stays on the same engine it used on-premises
explanation: Replatform makes a targeted optimization, such as moving to a managed database like RDS, to gain operational benefits without changing the application's core architecture. Refactor (re-architect) goes further, redesigning the application, often to be cloud-native, which is a bigger change than replatforming. Repurchase means switching to a different product entirely, such as moving to a SaaS offering, which is not what happens here. Rehost involves no changes at all, but adopting a managed database is itself a change, so this is not rehosting. Retain means keeping a workload on-premises rather than migrating it, which contradicts moving to RDS.

stem: A company is designing its disaster recovery approach for a critical workload and is comparing AWS DR strategies. Which TWO of the following correctly describe valid AWS disaster recovery strategies? (Select TWO.)
options: Multi-Region active-active is the lowest-cost strategy because it needs no standby infrastructure at all.
Backup and restore is the lowest-cost, highest-recovery-time strategy, where data is backed up and infrastructure is provisioned only after a disaster occurs.
Pilot light requires a fully scaled duplicate of production running at all times in a second Region.
Warm standby means production traffic is already split evenly across two Regions before any disaster occurs.
Pilot light keeps a minimal version of core systems always running in a second Region so recovery can scale that environment up quickly during a disaster.
explanation: Backup and restore is the lowest-cost, slowest strategy: data is backed up, and compute infrastructure is only stood up after a disaster is declared. Pilot light keeps a minimal, always-on copy of core systems, such as a replicated database, in a second Region, so that during a disaster the rest of the environment can be scaled up around that core quickly. Multi-Region active-active is actually the most expensive and complex strategy, not the cheapest, since it runs full production capacity in multiple Regions simultaneously. Running a fully scaled duplicate at all times describes warm standby or active-active, not pilot light. Warm standby means a scaled-down but fully functional copy runs continuously, not an even split of live production traffic.

stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following is AWS's responsibility, described as security 'of' the cloud?
options: The physical security of data centers, and the host infrastructure, including the hardware, software, networking, and facilities that run all AWS services
Configuring IAM users, groups, and permissions within a customer's own AWS account
Encrypting the customer's application data and managing the customer's encryption keys
Patching the guest operating system running on a customer's EC2 instances
explanation: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud: the physical facilities, hardware, and the underlying host infrastructure, software, and networking that run every AWS service. Configuring IAM permissions, managing customer-controlled encryption and keys, and patching the guest OS on EC2 are all customer responsibilities, security in the cloud, because the customer controls how those resources are configured and used.

stem: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following is the CUSTOMER's responsibility?
options: Maintaining and replacing the physical servers and networking hardware in the data center
Patching the guest operating system, configuring security group rules, and managing IAM permissions for the application
Ensuring the physical data center has redundant power and environmental controls
Decommissioning and securely disposing of storage hardware at end of life
explanation: The customer is responsible for security in the cloud: patching the guest OS, configuring network controls such as security groups, and managing IAM identities and permissions for their own resources. Maintaining physical servers, data center power and environmental controls, and disposing of retired storage hardware are all part of AWS's security of the cloud responsibility, since AWS controls the underlying facilities.

stem: A company compares running a database on a self-managed EC2 instance versus running the same database engine on Amazon RDS. Which statement correctly describes how the shared responsibility model shifts for a managed service like RDS?
options: There is no difference; the customer patches the underlying operating system in both cases
AWS becomes responsible for the customer's application-level data and query logic in both cases
AWS takes on responsibility for patching the underlying operating system and database engine on RDS, which the customer would otherwise have to patch themselves on EC2
Using RDS removes the customer's responsibility for configuring security groups and IAM permissions
explanation: For managed services like Amazon RDS, AWS takes on more of the operational burden, including patching the underlying operating system and the database engine software, tasks the customer would otherwise have to handle on a self-managed EC2 database. AWS never takes responsibility for the customer's application data or query logic. Even with RDS, the customer still configures security groups, IAM permissions, and database-level access control, so those responsibilities do not disappear.

stem: Which TWO of the following are customer responsibilities under the AWS shared responsibility model? (Select TWO.)
options: Encrypting data and choosing how encryption keys are managed for the customer's own applications
Maintaining the physical security of the AWS data centers
Managing IAM users, groups, roles, and their permissions within the customer's account
Patching the hypervisor that underlies the EC2 service
Ensuring the global network backbone connecting AWS Regions is available
explanation: Customers are responsible for encrypting their own data and choosing how to manage the keys used to do it, and for managing IAM identities and permissions within their account. AWS, not the customer, secures the physical data centers, patches the underlying hypervisor, and maintains the global network backbone connecting Regions, since those are part of the infrastructure AWS operates.

stem: A company just created a new AWS account. Which practice reflects AWS's recommended way to protect the account's root user?
options: Share the root user credentials with every engineer so anyone can perform administrative tasks
Generate long-lived access keys for the root user and embed them in application code
Use the root user for daily administrative tasks because it always has full permissions
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user and use it only for tasks that require it, creating an IAM administrator for daily work
explanation: AWS recommends enabling MFA on the root user and reserving it only for the small set of tasks that truly require root, while creating an IAM administrator user for day-to-day administrative work. Sharing root credentials across a team, creating long-lived root access keys, and using root for routine tasks all increase the blast radius if credentials are compromised, which is exactly what these practices avoid.

stem: An application running on an EC2 instance needs to read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. AWS best practice is to avoid storing long-lived access keys on the instance. Which approach follows this best practice?
options: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance that grants the permissions needed to access the S3 bucket
Create an IAM user with an access key and secret key, and hardcode the keys into the application
Store the AWS root user's access key in the instance's environment variables
Disable IAM entirely and rely on the S3 bucket being publicly readable
explanation: An IAM role attached to the EC2 instance provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials to the application with no long-lived keys stored anywhere, which is the AWS best practice. Hardcoding an IAM user's access key or the root user's key into an application or its environment creates long-lived secrets that can leak, and making the bucket public removes access control rather than managing it correctly.

stem: A developer needs permission to upload files to a single Amazon S3 bucket used for a specific project, and nothing else. Which IAM approach follows the principle of least privilege?
options: Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy so the developer never runs into a permissions error
Create a policy that grants only the s3:PutObject action on that one specific bucket
Add the developer as a co-owner of the AWS account
Grant full access to all S3 buckets in the account so the developer can also use other buckets later if needed
explanation: Least privilege means granting only the specific permissions needed for the task, so a policy scoped to s3:PutObject on the one required bucket is correct. AdministratorAccess, account co-ownership, and account-wide S3 access all grant far more than the task requires, increasing risk if the developer's credentials are ever compromised.

stem: Which statement BEST describes the security benefit of enabling multi-factor authentication (MFA) on an AWS account?
options: It automatically encrypts all data stored by that account
It replaces the need for IAM policies entirely
It requires a second, independent factor, such as a code from a hardware or virtual device, in addition to the password, so a stolen password alone cannot be used to sign in
It grants the account additional AWS Free Tier usage
explanation: MFA adds a second authentication factor beyond the password, so an attacker who only has the password still cannot sign in, which significantly reduces the risk of account compromise from credential theft. MFA does not encrypt data, does not replace IAM policies (which still control what an authenticated identity can do), and has no effect on Free Tier usage.

stem: A company manages dozens of AWS accounts under AWS Organizations and wants to enforce a rule across every account in a particular organizational unit, such as preventing any account from disabling CloudTrail, regardless of what IAM permissions an individual user is granted. Which feature enforces this?
options: IAM user policies attached to each individual user in every account
Amazon GuardDuty findings
AWS Trusted Advisor recommendations
A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached to the organizational unit, which sets the maximum available permissions for all accounts under it
explanation: A Service Control Policy (SCP) attached at the organizational unit or account level sets the maximum permissions available to every account underneath it, so even an account administrator with an IAM policy that allows an action cannot perform it if an SCP denies it. IAM user policies only affect individual users and cannot enforce an organization-wide guardrail. GuardDuty detects threats and Trusted Advisor gives recommendations, but neither one enforces a permission boundary.

stem: A company's compliance team needs to download AWS's ISO certifications and SOC reports to satisfy an internal audit. Which AWS service provides self-service access to this compliance documentation?
options: AWS Artifact
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
AWS Trusted Advisor
explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for on-demand access to AWS's compliance reports, such as ISO certifications and SOC reports, and for reviewing and accepting agreements like the Business Associate Addendum. AWS Config tracks the configuration of a customer's own resources, Amazon Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor gives account-level recommendations, none of which provide AWS's compliance certification documents.

stem: A security team wants to continuously record the configuration of their AWS resources over time and be notified when a resource's configuration drifts from an approved baseline, such as an S3 bucket becoming publicly accessible. Which service provides this?
options: AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config, which records resource configuration history and evaluates resources against configuration rules
Amazon CloudWatch Logs
AWS Direct Connect
explanation: AWS Config continuously records the configuration state of resources and evaluates them against rules, flagging drift such as an S3 bucket becoming public. CloudTrail records API calls (who did what and when) rather than the resulting configuration state. CloudWatch Logs stores application and system logs, not resource configuration history. Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection and has nothing to do with configuration monitoring.

stem: After a security incident, an administrator needs to determine exactly which IAM user made a specific API call, from what IP address, and at what time. Which AWS service provides this record?
options: Amazon GuardDuty
AWS Config
AWS CloudTrail, which logs API calls made in the account, including the caller identity, source, and time
Amazon Macie
explanation: AWS CloudTrail records API activity across an AWS account, including who made each call, from where, and when, providing the audit trail needed to investigate an incident. GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that analyzes signals like CloudTrail events but does not itself store the raw call log. AWS Config tracks resource configuration rather than API call identity. Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, unrelated to API auditing.

stem: A security team wants a managed service that continuously analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events using threat intelligence and machine learning to detect suspicious activity, such as a compromised EC2 instance communicating with a known malicious IP address, without the team deploying any agents. Which service fits this need?
options: AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
AWS Firewall Manager
Amazon GuardDuty, which continuously analyzes account and network activity for threats using threat intelligence and machine learning
explanation: Amazon GuardDuty continuously monitors VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events with threat intelligence feeds and machine learning to surface findings like communication with a known malicious IP, requiring no agents to deploy. AWS Config tracks configuration compliance, not threat detection. Amazon Inspector scans EC2 and container images for software vulnerabilities. AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall rules across accounts, but it does not analyze logs for threat findings the way GuardDuty does.

stem: A network administrator configures a security group to allow inbound traffic on port 443 to a web server, but adds no outbound rule. Separately, a network ACL on the same subnet allows inbound traffic on port 443 but has no explicit outbound rule allowing the response traffic. What happens to the response traffic leaving the instance in each case?
options: The security group automatically allows the response traffic out because security groups are stateful, but the network ACL blocks it because network ACLs are stateless and require an explicit outbound rule
Both the security group and the network ACL automatically allow the response traffic, since both are stateful
Both the security group and the network ACL block the response traffic, since both require explicit outbound rules
The network ACL automatically allows the response traffic because it is stateful, but the security group blocks it because it is stateless
explanation: Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for an allowed inbound request is automatically permitted out, with no separate outbound rule needed. Network ACLs are stateless, so an explicit outbound rule is required to allow the response traffic to leave the subnet, even if the matching inbound request was allowed. It is the security group, not the ACL, that behaves statefully, and the ACL, not the security group, that requires the explicit rule, which is the opposite of what the other options claim.

stem: A company runs a public web application and wants to both filter incoming HTTP requests for common attack patterns like SQL injection, and protect against volumetric distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. Which TWO AWS services together address these needs? (Select TWO.)
options: AWS Config, to detect malicious HTTP request patterns
AWS WAF, to filter web requests using rules that block patterns like SQL injection and cross-site scripting
Amazon Macie, to protect against DDoS attacks
AWS Shield, to protect against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks
AWS Trusted Advisor, to block malicious web requests in real time
explanation: AWS WAF lets you write rules that inspect HTTP requests and block patterns such as SQL injection or cross-site scripting, and AWS Shield provides protection against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, together covering both requirements. AWS Config tracks resource configuration and does not inspect HTTP request content. Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3 and has no DDoS protection function. AWS Trusted Advisor gives account recommendations; it does not block malicious requests in real time.

stem: A company wants to encrypt data stored in Amazon S3 and Amazon EBS using encryption keys that it can centrally create, rotate, and control access to through IAM policies, without managing its own key-management hardware. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Certificate Manager
AWS Key Management Service (KMS), which lets customers create and control encryption keys used to protect their data
Amazon Macie
AWS Secrets Manager
explanation: AWS KMS lets customers create, manage, rotate, and control access to the encryption keys used to protect data in services like S3 and EBS, without operating their own key-management hardware. AWS Certificate Manager issues and manages TLS/SSL certificates, a different function from managing data-encryption keys. Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data rather than managing keys. AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates application secrets like database credentials, not general-purpose encryption keys for S3 or EBS.

stem: An application stores a database password that must be automatically rotated on a schedule, with the rotation logic integrated directly into the service so the credential in use is always current. Which AWS service is purpose-built for automatic secret rotation like this?
options: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, which is the only option that supports any form of automatic rotation
Amazon S3 with server-side encryption enabled
AWS Secrets Manager, which natively supports automatic, scheduled rotation of secrets such as database credentials
AWS CloudHSM, which is designed specifically for storing and rotating application secrets
explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built to store secrets like database credentials and natively supports automatic, scheduled rotation, including built-in integration with services such as Amazon RDS. Systems Manager Parameter Store can store configuration values and secrets but does not provide native automatic rotation the way Secrets Manager does. S3 with server-side encryption protects stored objects, not credential rotation. AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for key storage and cryptographic operations, not a secrets-rotation service.

stem: A data governance team wants to automatically scan the objects in an Amazon S3 bucket to discover and classify sensitive data, such as personally identifiable information (PII) like names and social security numbers. Which AWS service is designed for this?
options: AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon Macie, which uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII in Amazon S3
explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and classify sensitive data, including PII, stored in Amazon S3. AWS Config tracks resource configuration rather than data content. Amazon GuardDuty detects threats from account and network activity, not sensitive-data discovery. AWS CloudTrail logs API activity, unrelated to scanning object content for PII.

stem: A company wants to serve its public website over HTTPS and needs a TLS/SSL certificate that AWS can automatically renew before it expires, at no additional cost for the certificate itself, for use with an Application Load Balancer or CloudFront distribution. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), which provisions and automatically renews public TLS/SSL certificates for use with integrated AWS services
AWS Key Management Service (KMS)
AWS Secrets Manager
Amazon Macie
explanation: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions public TLS/SSL certificates at no additional cost and automatically renews them, and it integrates directly with services like Application Load Balancer and CloudFront to enable HTTPS. AWS KMS manages encryption keys for data at rest, not public TLS certificates. AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates application secrets such as database credentials, a different use case than issuing public certificates. Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, unrelated to certificate management.
